doc.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Making the first album: Bob Russell and picking her songs
summary: Bob Russell arranged for Benny Carter and Marty Paich; she chose the songs and built the album around a love story gone bad, though she was not yet writing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How did you -- when you did the album in '56 with the Benny Carter arrangement and Marty Page and Benny Carter, -­

That was Bob Russell who did that. It's always been for me like that. After Bob, it was Max and now there's Jean-Philippe Allard, somebody to help me to think because I don't know these musicians. I didn't know who Marty Page was or, I mean, I heard his name, but I wouldn't have thought to ask Benny Carter to do this.
How did this -- when you got these arrangements, when you started to work on that, was it different from what you'd done in the past musically?
It's just the same music, but no, I wasn't overwhelmed or anything.

I had to learn the song and sing it the best I could and that's what everybody else was doing. They played what Benny wrote the best they could, and I was singing. I picked the greatest songs I could find because I was making peace with Bob. He wrote "Do Nothing Till You Hear From Me." He wrote "Crazy He Calls Me." He wrote "No More." He wrote all these songs and including the title song "Affair," and I came up with the idea of the love story of a girl, a love song, a love story that goes bad because all I ever knew was about a love affair that went bad, and so because I've always picked the songs I would sing, people don't pick my material. They may pick the musicians, help me pick the musicians, but I pick the songs.
Were you writing yet your own lyrics?
Were you thinking about it? Starting writing?

I wasn't thinking about it. I didn't know I could write, but because Bob had introduced me to these great writers, I knew what a great writer was. He told me a great song is succinct, it's original, yeah, and he's a great -- he was a great songwriter. "Would I Love You?" Yeah. "No More" with Tudy Camaradi.
